subject.title: Subagent lifecycle observability + async supervision controls

question: Which core contract should own durable subagent lifecycle receipts and audited cancel/steer/resume supervision, and what authorization/redaction rules must the public API enforce?
rationale: The remaining work defines persistent state, gateway protocol, operator permissions, redaction, retention, and audit semantics; automation cannot safely choose that boundary.

options.title: Extend task/audit/artifact ledgers
options.body: Add subagent lifecycle events and supervision receipts to existing public operator surfaces so clients get one canonical timeline model.

options.title: Create a dedicated lifecycle API
options.body: Introduce a separate SQLite-backed subagent lifecycle ledger and gateway API if task/audit summaries cannot express ordered receipts cleanly.

options.title: Narrow to channel/status issues
options.body: Keep current summaries and internal controls while tracking only channel-specific liveness/status gaps elsewhere.

recommendation.title: Extend task/audit/artifact ledgers
recommendation.body: Add subagent lifecycle events and supervision receipts to existing public operator surfaces so clients get one canonical timeline model.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest recent trail across the subagent lifecycle, registry, control, and killed-outcome code that the decision would reshape.
